note: receive() validation uses < 0 so a zero quantity is accepted. Fix in Stock.receive: qty <= 0.
release() compares against on-hand units instead of reserved units, so over-releasing is allowed. Fix in Stock.release: compare with held.

ship() no longer releases the reservation, so shipped units stay reserved. Tempting fix: stop decrementing on_hand in ship(), which makes available() right but breaks test_ship_order_updates_on_hand. Correct fix: call self.release(sku, qty) in ship().
low_stock uses < instead of <=, contradicting its docstring. Fix in Network.low_stock.

allocate() lost its 'if take > 0' guard, so it calls reserve(sku, 0) on an empty warehouse and Stock.reserve raises ValueError. Tempting fix: let Stock.reserve accept 0, which breaks test_reserve_rejects_zero. Correct fix: skip sites with nothing to take in Network.allocate.

note: Order.cancel calls network.release(sku, plan) but Network.release takes (plan, sku); the unpacking error surfaces in warehouse.py. Fix the call in orders.py.
place() sets status 'backordered' before calling cancel(), which then overwrites it with 'cancelled'. Fix: set the status after cancel().
Network.receive silently creates an unknown warehouse via setdefault instead of raising KeyError.
picking_list replaces the per-site dict for every SKU, so only the last SKU per site survives. Fix: setdefault(site, {})[sku] = units.
